subject: Evaluation brief: recommended model slate, runtime profiles, and bench links
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@novacorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation brief: recommended model slate, runtime profiles, and bench links

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Per our conversation, I put together a short evaluation brief with the model slate we recommend for NovaCorp's doc-summarization + snippet-retrieval flow, plus Redwood-verified runtime profiles and the key bench evidence you asked for. Short summary up front, then links and next steps.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Recommended primary model: orca-13b-redwood-q4 — best balance for NanoSearch workload with embeddings-backed retrieval; verified 320 TPS aggregate on our p2-standard cluster with 256-token context.
- Cost-lean fallback: llama-3-8b-quant — ~760 TPS, slightly higher p99 (165 ms) but lower per-token cost for high-throughput batches.
- Suggested pilot: 2-week A/B: orca-13b-redwood-q4 vs llama-3-8b-quant on a 5k-query/day slice (real queries + seeded prompt set). Measure p50/p90/p99 latency, end-to-end request success, and summary-quality delta on your evaluation set.

Redwood-verified runtime profiles (attached CSV + dashboard link)
- orca-13b-redwood-q4: TPS (avg): 320; latency p50: 22 ms; p90: 48 ms; p99: 120 ms; GPU: a100-80GB; batching policy: 48/8/2 (continuous batching tuned to 256-token avg).
- llama-3-8b-quant: TPS (avg): 760; latency p50: 12 ms; p90: 38 ms; p99: 165 ms; GPU: t4-like quantized path; batching policy: 128/16/4.
- oracle-high-32k: for long-context sessions (optional): TPS: 58; p50: 120 ms; p90: 270 ms; p99: 640 ms (recommend for long-doc summarization runs only).

Bench links and artifacts
- Redwood benchmark dashboard (live traces + percentile calc): https://redwood.app/dashboard/benchmarks/DEAL-9921
- Prompt set & evaluation pack (seeded queries + quality rubric): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExamplePromptset
- Attached: novacorp-eval-promptset-v1.txt (prompt set), redwood-verified-profiles-aug2026.csv (runtime profiles, hardware details, batching configs)

Quality/regression concerns and guardrails
- We recommend guard rails for prompt drift: save top 500 failing prompts weekly, monitor delta on Rouge/BLEU-like metric you prefer, and add a regression alert when mean summary quality drops >4% vs baseline.
- Fallbacks: Canary route to llama-3-8b-quant if p99 crosses 300 ms for >2 min; automatic rollback policy in the Redwood Console will cut traffic to fallback model and alert your SRE.

Suggested next steps
1) Confirm pilot scope & sample size (5k queries/day or reduce to 2k for narrower run).
2) Provide a read-only S3/Drive location for us to drop traces and collected outputs (we need this to populate the evaluation dashboard).
3) Schedule a short kickoff (20 min) to map metric ownership and hand off prompt set.

Open questions for you
- Do you have an internal quality threshold (e.g., minimum acceptable summary F1) that we should use for pass/fail?
- Any constraints on GPU types / region (we saw you asked about us-east vs eu-west)?

I'll loop in Karthik to propose the pilot infra config and Marcus to own the benchmark delivery.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Subject: Re: Evaluation brief: recommended model slate, runtime profiles, and bench links

Neha —

Thanks, this is great and very actionable. Quick clarifying Qs:
1) For the pilot, can we cap to 2k queries/day to start? Procurement wants to limit spend until we see quality.
2) On the fallback threshold: when you say \"p99 crosses 300 ms for >2 min\", does Redwood provide automated remediation or do we need an SRE runbook?

On the quality threshold, Sarah prefers a pragmatic approach: baseline Rouge ~0.62 on our seed set; anything below 0.58 should trigger a deeper review.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Jordan / Sarah —

Thanks for the quick replies. Agree on starting smaller — 2k queries/day pilot works. To your remediation question: Redwood provides automated remediation out of the box (we'll configure the canary and the p99 trigger), but we also recommend a one-page SRE runbook in your Ops space for the first pilot (fast restore steps, who to page, and how to interpret the Console traces). We'll drop a template runbook into the shared Drive folder today.

Action items I will take by EOD:
- Karthik will provision the pilot infra and share the exact cluster spec + expected monthly estimate.
- Marcus will push the first bench snapshot to the dashboard (you'll see live TPS and percentile traces) and attach the proof CSV.
- I'll add the Redwood automation policy (canary thresholds + rollback) to the Drive folder and tag Sarah + procurement.

Can we do a 20-min kickoff tomorrow at 10:00 am PT? If that works I'll send a calendar invite with the agenda: scope, metrics, data handoff, and quick acceptance criteria.

Thanks — looking forward.

Neha Kapoor
